desc.zh: 美国独立战争中华盛顿亲自组建的间谍圈，用数字代号与隐形墨水传递英军情报；代号密信与密码本至今藏于美国国家档案馆。
desc.en: A spy ring personally formed by George Washington during the American Revolution, trading British intelligence in numeric codes and invisible ink; the coded letters and codebook survive in the U.S. National Archives.

text.zh: 代号「711」是华盛顿本人，「71」是英军统帅克林顿，「355」是一位女谍；密信夹藏于商业信件行间，以隐形墨水显形，成就独立战争最传奇的情报网。
text.en: Code 711 meant Washington himself, 71 the British commander Clinton, and 355 a female agent; messages hidden between the lines of business letters surfaced with sympathetic ink — the Revolution's most legendary spy ring.

desc.zh: 法国密码学家巴泽里重造的轮式密码：二十枚乱序字母圆盘穿于同一轴，对齐转动即可加解密；1901 年被法国陆军列装，服役至一战。
desc.en: French cryptanalyst Étienne Bazeries reinvented the wheel cipher — twenty scrambled-letter disks on one rod, aligned and rotated to encipher; adopted by the French Army in 1901 and still in service during WWI.

text.zh: 1891 年巴泽里把二十枚乱序字母圆盘串于一轴，收发双方对齐明文与密文行即完成加密；法军以「密码圆筒」之名列装，与杰斐逊轮式密码异曲同工。
text.en: In 1891 Bazeries threaded twenty scrambled-letter disks onto one rod: sender and receiver align plaintext and ciphertext rows and the code appears on the other row; the French Army fielded it as the “cipher cylinder,” echoing Jefferson's wheel cypher.

desc.zh: 谢尔比乌斯推向市场的民用转子密码机，曾在伯尔尼万国邮政大会公开演示；它没有插线板、密钥空间有限，却是德军军用恩尼格玛的直系前身。
desc.en: Scherbius's civilian rotor machine, publicly demonstrated at the Bern Postal Congress; without a plugboard its key space was limited, yet it was the direct ancestor of the military Enigma.

text.zh: 1923 年谢尔比乌斯携恩尼格玛 D 型亮相伯尔尼邮政大会，向各国推销这台「无法破译」的机器；德军以它为蓝本加装插线板改出军用型，日后让布莱切利园吃尽苦头。
text.en: In 1923 Scherbius presented the Enigma D at the Bern Postal Congress, pitching an “unbreakable” machine to the world's postal services; the Reichswehr rebuilt that commercial design with a plugboard into the military Enigma that would torment Bletchley Park.

desc.zh: 美国海军陆战队以纳瓦霍语编制两套密码，训练纳瓦霍人担任无线电通讯员；日军始终无法破解，硫磺岛六名译电员 48 小时无差错收发 800 余条电文。
desc.en: The U.S. Marine Corps built two codebooks on the Navajo language and trained Navajo speakers as radio operators; the Japanese never broke it — at Iwo Jima six code talkers relayed over 800 error-free messages in 48 hours.

text.zh: 初版密码仅 211 词：战斗机叫「蜂鸟」，潜艇叫「铁鱼」，战列舰叫「鲸鱼」；硫磺岛六名译电员 48 小时收发 800 余条电文，无一差错。
text.en: The original code held just 211 words: a fighter was “hummingbird,” a submarine “iron fish,” a battleship “whale”; at Iwo Jima six operators passed 800-plus messages in 48 hours without a single error.

name.zh: 中世纪修道院密写字母

desc.zh: 中世纪抄经修士以符文式替代字母在羊皮纸上藏写署名与批注；16 世纪初修道院院长特里特米乌斯更创制多套「天使字母表」，开西方密码学著作之先河。
desc.en: Medieval scribes hid signatures and glosses on parchment in rune-like substitution alphabets; in the early 1500s Abbot Trithemius went further, inventing “angelic alphabets” that launched Western cryptographic literature.

text.zh: 修士在古英语手稿里用符文替换拉丁字母，把署名藏进寻常抄本；1518 年特里特米乌斯出版《多文书写法》，创制多套「天使字母」，开西方密码学著作先河。
text.en: In Old English manuscripts monks swapped Anglo-Saxon runes for Latin letters, burying signatures inside ordinary-looking codices; in 1518 Trithemius published Polygraphia with invented “angelic” alphabets, among the first books of cryptography.

desc.zh: 南北战争联邦军信号兵团使用的双盘式密码盘：两枚同心铜盘错位旋转即完成字母替换；南军多次破译其电文，迫使联邦不断更换密钥与用法。
desc.en: The twin-disk device of the Union Signal Corps: two concentric brass rings rotated against each other to substitute letters; Confederate codebreakers repeatedly read its traffic, forcing constant changes in Union practice.

text.zh: 两盘同心铜盘，外盘为正常字母，内盘乱序；转动至约定偏移后逐字替换。战争中南军多次破译其电文，联邦军被迫频繁更换密钥，密盘遂成联邦信号密码的象征。
text.en: Two concentric brass disks — a normal outer alphabet, a scrambled inner one — slid to an agreed shift for letter-by-letter substitution. Confederate codebreakers read its traffic more than once, so the Union kept changing keys; the disk became the emblem of federal signal ciphers.

era.zh: 1918 年 6 月 · 法国西线

desc.zh: 1918 年 6 月 3 日，法国密码专家佩恩万破译德军 ADFGVX 密电，读出「速运弹药，昼间亦无妨」等句，据此判明德军进攻方向，联军得以挫败六月攻势。
desc.en: On June 3, 1918, French cryptanalyst Georges Painvin broke a German ADFGVX message reading “Rush munitions. Even by day if not seen,” pinpointing the coming offensive so the Allies could blunt it.

text.zh: 德军 3 月启用 ADFGX，6 月换用含数字的 ADFGVX；佩恩万 6 月 3 日数小时破译密电：「速运弹药，昼间亦无妨」，判明主攻方向，为此瘦了 15 公斤。
text.en: The Germans fielded ADFGX in March and switched to the digit-adding ADFGVX on June 1; on June 3 Painvin decrypted a message within hours — “Rush munitions. Even by day if not seen” — revealing the offensive's focus. Cracking it cost him 15 kg.
